body.statement: At depth \(\ell\), every arm partition has fewer than \(8/h_\ell\) clusters, the residual basic table satisfies \(R_\ell<24/h_\ell\), and \(R_0=0\). The tree repair produces exact marginal multiplicities and its cross-child movement counts satisfy \(M_{a,\ell}\le R_{\ell+1}\) for every arm and every nonterminal depth. These conclusions hold with repeated atoms, arbitrarily small positive rational gaps, and slope intervals touching dyadic boundaries.
body.justification: This lemma turns sparse fractional residuals into exact same-size marginal counts without invoking a false bounded-discrepancy claim for three permutations.
body.gap: Haus (2015) gives exact and bottleneck algorithms for special matrix classes, while standard tensor rounding returns another fractional plan; neither controls same-size row repair along an optimal-support hierarchy.
body.consumer: The movement inequality is the combinatorial input for the universal additive cost guarantee.
